question: Smith (2023) Tables 6-7 and Smith (2025) Table 7, and the other tables of the gap audit of 26 November 2026 read with them (Robinson & Lobel 2013 Tables 4, 10; Blust 2013 Tables 8.20, 8.21, 8.24, 8.31; Smith 2017c Tables 2, 3, 8; Smith 2023 Tables 8-9): what is entered?
chosen_reading: Only the cells that were not yet rows. Miri *jʰ > s and *ɡʰ > k (Smith 2023, Table 6). Begak *ɡ > ɡ and ɡk after schwa, and *R > ∅ between vowels (Smith 2023, Table 7), the last beside the existing row *R > ɡ / V_V from Smith (2017a, Table 70), which it contradicts. From Smith (2025, Table 7), stated against PMP (parent_lect_id pmp): Havu *ay > e; Kambera *ay > i, *aw > u, *uy > i; Kedang *ay > e, *aw > o, *uy > i; Komodo and Sika *uy > i; Lio and Ngadha *ay > e beside the truncated reflex a that Proto-Central Flores already has. Everything else in the tables is already a row from Blust (2002, 2007), Smith (2017a), Mead (2003), Billings & McDonnell (2024), Nothofer (1975) or Grimes & Edwards (2026), or concerns a variety that is not a lect.
alternatives: Enter the Manggarai (*ay > a/i, *aw > o, *uy > i) and Lamaholot (*ay > a/e, *aw > a/o, *uy > i) rows of Smith (2025) Table 7 on Proto-Manggarai and Proto-Lamaholot, or on one dialect each; they are held back because Smith's 'Manggarai' and 'Lamaholot' name a language that is a proto-language with dialects here. Make lects of Lebo' Vo', Lepo' Tau and Penan (Smith 2023, Table 6), Long Anap Kenyah (Blust 2013, Table 8.20), Tiruray (Smith 2023, Table 9), Moken (Smith 2017c, Table 3), Kasiguranin and the Cagayan Valley languages (Robinson & Lobel 2013, Tables 4, 10). Restate the Proto-North Sarawak rows *b > *bʰ etc., now 'conditions unknown', with the conditions of Blust (2013: 557-558) and Smith (2023: 353): after penultimate schwa, and from assimilated clusters. Restate the Begak and Idaan rows bp, dt, ɡk (now sporadic, V_V) the same way, and replace Begak *R > ɡ / V_V by ∅. Enter the low vowel fronting of Robinson & Lobel's Table 4 language by language, with its lexemes (now one sporadic row on Proto-Northeastern Luzon). Smith (2017c) Table 2 has Karo -k for final *j; the Proto-Northern Batak row from Billings & McDonnell (2024) and Adelaar (1981) has -ŋ, and is left as it is.
